recentIncidents.headline: Munger Resident Duped in Fake KBC Tax Clearance Call
recentIncidents.publisher: Bihar Police Cyber Advisory Bulletin & I4C MHA
recentIncidents.summary: According to the official advisory, a victim received a fraudulent WhatsApp audio call pretending to be KBC support, demanding tax processing fees prior to prize disbursal.
recentIncidents.policeAction: FIR No. 42/2026 registered under IT Act Sec 66D & IPC Sec 420 at Munger Cyber Thana; target bank accounts & SIM cards frozen.
recentIncidents.fullReportText:
PAGE 1 — INCIDENT CASE STUDY & MODUS OPERANDI:

On 10 August 2026, an official incident report was lodged at the Munger Cyber Police Thana regarding a sophisticated lottery extortion scam. The victim received a high-priority WhatsApp audio call carrying an official-looking Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC) display badge and logo. The perpetrator claimed that the victim's mobile number had won a cash prize of ₹25 Lakh in a national lucky draw organized by KBC and telecom providers.

To establish false legitimacy, the scammer transmitted forged digital certificates featuring official government emblems, fake RBI approval seals, and bogus tax calculation vouchers. The victim was instructed that to disburse the net winning amount into their bank account, an immediate advance tax clearance fee of ₹1,80,000 had to be deposited into a designated National Tax Settlement account.

PAGE 2 — TECHNICAL ANATOMY, LEGAL ACTION & I4C PREVENTION ADVISORY:

Technical Threat Anatomy:
• Communication Vectors: VoIP WhatsApp Calls originating from spoofed Virtual Private Numbers (+92 / +44 country codes mapped to local numbers).
• Financial Routing: Funds were routed through 3 consecutive IMPS layer transactions into private mule accounts hosted at regional private sector banks in West Bengal and Delhi.
• Digital Artifacts: Fraudulent PDF vouchers titled 'KBC_Govt_Tax_Clearance_2026.pdf' containing embedded tracking scripts.

Law Enforcement Action Log:
• FIR Registered: FIR No. 42/2026 under Information Technology Act Section 66D and IPC Section 420 at Munger Cyber Police Thana.
• Asset Freezing: Munger Cyber Cell coordinated with the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCPRP) to freeze ₹1,45,000 across 2 mule bank accounts before final withdrawal.

Official Citizen Prevention Protocol (I4C Ministry of Home Affairs):
1. Neither KBC, Sony Entertainment, nor any legitimate organization demands advance GST or processing tax for lottery prizes.
2. Income Tax on lottery winnings (Section 194B) is deducted at source (TDS) by the organizer — victims NEVER need to pay tax upfront.
3. In case of financial fraud, immediately dial National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 within the Golden Hour to trigger automatic account freezing.

recentIncidents.headline: Digital Arrest Extortion Attempt Flagged in Boring Road Patna
recentIncidents.publisher: Patna Cyber Crime Police Branch & PIB Advisory
recentIncidents.summary: Scammers impersonating TRAI regulatory officers and CBI officials placed a victim under 14-hour video lock-in under threat of illegal parcel narcotics charges.
recentIncidents.policeAction: Patna Cyber Police Thana registered FIR under IT Act Sec 66D & BNS Sec 318(4); 4 mule accounts frozen.
recentIncidents.fullReportText:
PAGE 1 — INCIDENT CASE STUDY & MODUS OPERANDI:

A severe Digital Arrest extortion racket targeting senior citizens and working professionals was neutralized by the Patna Cyber Police Branch on 09 August 2026 in the Boring Road area of Patna. The victim received an automated IVR call claiming that their primary mobile SIM card was being disconnected within 2 hours due to 18 registered illegal gambling and money laundering complaints.

Upon pressing '9' to speak with a representative, the call was transferred to an operative posing as an officer of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI). The operative alleged that a courier parcel containing 5 illegal passports, 150 grams of MDMA narcotics, and 3 forged bank cards sent from Mumbai to Taiwan was seized under the victim's Aadhaar credentials.

The victim was then subjected to a 14-hour high-pressure Skype video call with cybercriminals dressed in fake police uniforms sitting in a room styled like a police station. The criminals issued a forged 'Digital Arrest Order' signed in the name of the Chief Justice of India and coerced the victim into transferring ₹14,50,000 under the pretext of 'Supreme Court RBI Verification Escrow'.

PAGE 2 — TECHNICAL ANATOMY, LEGAL ACTION & I4C PREVENTION ADVISORY:

Technical Threat Anatomy:
• Communication Vectors: Skype Video Call handle 'cbi.investigation.dept.gov' using artificial background studio setups.
• Financial Routing: Funds transferred via RTGS into 4 shell company accounts registered in NCR and Kolkata.

Law Enforcement Action Log:
• FIR Details: FIR registered under IT Act Section 66D and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Section 318(4) at Patna Cyber Crime Police Thana.
• Account Freezing: Cyber Cell triggered 1930 portal inter-bank protocols, successfully freezing ₹11,20,000 across 3 recipient bank accounts.

Official Citizen Prevention Protocol (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre - I4C):
1. 'Digital Arrest' DOES NOT EXIST in Indian Law. No police force, CBI, ED, Customs, or TRAI conducts interrogation or arrest over Skype/WhatsApp video calls.
2. Police officers will NEVER demand money or funds transfer into 'safety escrow' accounts.
3. If you receive any video call threatening arrest, immediately disconnect, block the number, and report to Cyber Crime Helpline 1930.
